SEARCH
Package org.smtlib

Class AbstractSolver

java.lang.Object
org.smtlib.AbstractSolver
All Implemented Interfaces:
ISolver
Direct Known Subclasses:
Solver_altergo, Solver_bitwuzla, Solver_cvc5, Solver_simplify, Solver_smt, Solver_smtinterpol, Solver_z3_4_3, Solver_z3_recent
public class AbstractSolver extends Object implements ISolver
This class implements the operations of the org.smtlib.ISolver interface that map directly onto a single translated command sent to the solver process, with the expected response of a fully SMT-LIB compliant solver (a flat success/error/sat/unsat/ unknown/unsupported, or a bare value/attribute-pair for get-option/get-info): the command is translated with translate(INode) and sent via sendCommand(ICommand). get_assertions/get_value/get_assignment/get_unsat_core/ get_unsat_assumptions additionally reparse a non-flat response as the structured list they're actually specified to return (a (term value) pair list, a name list, etc. — see Parser.parseValueList() and its siblings), since parseResponse(String)'s generic parse only handles flat outcomes and just returns a raw s-expression for anything else. A subclass whose target solver deviates from strict SMT-LIB concrete syntax or response format overrides translate(INode) and/or parseResponse(String); a subclass whose target solver deviates in some other way overrides the individual ISolver method itself, same as before.

start() still throws UnsupportedOperationException, because AbstractSolver has no generic way to provide it: constructing the solver process and choosing its command line is inherently solver-specific, so every concrete adapter must override it. exit(), by contrast, has a working default (send the exit command tolerating a silent process exit, then tear down the process) that's generic enough to cover every solver seen so far; a subclass only overrides it when exiting needs solver-specific handling beyond that.

Thus this class can still be used as a base class for a solver adapter class that wants the convenience of not having to implement every operation at once (remove AbstractSolver as a base class and retain ISolver as an interface to check that all ISolver methods are indeed present in the derived class), while getting working default behavior for the operations that don't need solver-specific handling.

Author:
David Cok

    • linesOffset

      protected int linesOffset
      The correction to a line number the solver reports for the command whose response is being read: line N of the solver's input is shown as line N - linesOffset, the line of the user's source on which that command starts. The solver numbers the lines it receives, which are not the source's: jSMTLIB adds lines (a priming :print-success, a pipelining barrier, an adapter's own query), omits lines (blank lines, commands answered here) and sends each command on one line. So rather than tracking each such difference, linesOffset is set by sendScriptText(boolean, java.lang.String...) whenever text is sent for a command of the script, from the solver line that text starts on and the command's source line (see setSourceLine(int)). A command without a source line (one built through the API) counts as the line after the previous one. An adapter rewrites the line numbers in its solver's messages with withSourceLines(java.lang.String).

    • selfReportsImmediateExit

      protected boolean selfReportsImmediateExit()
      Overridden by a subclass whose target solver's :error-behavior is immediate-exit (e.g. cvc5, yices2) rather than the SMT-LIB default of continued-execution -- such a solver's process may start exiting asynchronously right after it reports an error, and SolverProcess.send(boolean, String...)'s own process.isAlive() check can still read true for a brief window afterward (OS process-death bookkeeping lags the actual exit) -- see sendCommand(ICommand, boolean), which uses this to give a solver that just reported an error a moment to actually finish dying before the next command's liveness check runs, closing that race deterministically rather than guessing from the error's content whether the process will actually exit.

    • checkImmediateExit

      protected IResponse checkImmediateExit(IResponse result)
      Called with each response parsed from the solver. After an error response from a selfReportsImmediateExit() solver, gives its process a moment to finish exiting (see IMMEDIATE_EXIT_SETTLE_MILLIS). If the error is one after which the solver no longer processes input (errorStopsSolver(IResponse)) and the process is still alive, it is stopped, since a later command -- or exit() -- would otherwise wait forever for a reply. Only the OS process is stopped; the adapter is left as it is, so later commands answer that the solver process has exited and exit() cleans up normally.

    • errorStopsSolver

      protected String translate(INode sexpr) throws IVisitor.VisitorException
      Translates an in-memory node into the text sent to the solver process. The base behavior assumes the solver is fully SMT-LIB compliant, so it is exactly what the default printer produces. Override in a subclass whose target solver deviates from strict SMT-LIB concrete syntax.
      Throws:

    • parseResponse

      protected IResponse parseResponse(String response)
      Parses the solver's raw response text. The base behavior assumes the response is exactly standard SMT-LIB concrete syntax: success/sat/unsat/unknown/unsupported/ true/false, an (error "...") s-expression, a bare value (get-option), or a single (:keyword value) attribute pair (get-info). It does not build the richer structured IResponse subtypes that get_value/get_model/get_proof/ get_assertions/get_unsat_core/get_unsat_assumptions/get_assignment need, nor does it correct for any real solver's non-compliant quirks (e.g. legacy bit-vector literal syntax) — override in a subclass whose target solver needs either.

    • sendCommand

      protected IResponse sendCommand(ICommand cmd)
      Translates the given command and sends it to the solver process, returning the parsed response. This is the mechanism behind the default implementations below; a subclass may also call it directly to send a command built some other way.

      protected IResponse sendExitCommand()
      Sends the exit command, tolerating the solver producing literally no response (SolverProcess.NoResponseException) as a benign, expected outcome rather than an error -- many solvers legitimately print nothing before terminating in response to exit. The tolerated result is "", which Parser.parseResponse("") already turns into a plain empty response -- the same outcome a real empty response (e.g. under :print-success false) already produces, so no separate response-construction case is needed here. A subclass's exit() should call this instead of sendCommand(commandFactory.exit()) directly.

    • normalizeForTesting

      protected static String normalizeForTesting(String raw, IExpr.IKeyword infoflag)
      Replaces known sources of non-deterministic content in a raw solver response with a fixed placeholder, so that --testing runs produce byte-for-byte reproducible output across machines and repeated runs. Deliberately a short, explicit list rather than a broad catch-all, so it can't silently mask an actual difference in solver output: elapsed-time figures (e.g. cvc5's :all-statistics response embeds these as bare, unquoted "NNNms" tokens, which aren't valid SMT-LIB syntax at all and would otherwise cascade into a wall of "Invalid token" parse errors that also differ every run), and, in a reply to get-info :all-statistics, every number: statistics are run-dependent by nature, and solvers name them as they please. Their names are kept.

    • pipelines

      public boolean pipelines(ICommand cmd)
      Whether sendPipelined(ICommand) may send the command without waiting for its response. True for the commands whose execution here sends the command (once) and has nothing to do with its response beyond returning it -- except check-sat, whose response becomes checkSatStatus when it is read. A subclass returns false for a command whose solver response needs correcting before it is compliant, or that it executes otherwise, and for all commands if it does not send them through sendCommand.

    • sendPipelined

      public IResponse sendPipelined(ICommand cmd)
      Executes a command for which pipelines(ICommand) is true, sending it to the solver without waiting for the response. Returns a AbstractSolver.Pending response if the command was sent, or the actual response if it was not (e.g. an error found before sending). Any other request to this solver first waits for the pending responses, but a caller must call readPipelined(boolean) with true itself before executing a command that is checked against an earlier response (such as get-value against check-sat).

    • executePipelined

      public IResponse executePipelined(List<ICommand> commands)
      Executes the commands in order, as a script does: returns the first error, or else the last command's response. Commands that pipelines(ICommand) allows are sent without waiting for their responses; check-sat, check-sat-assuming and every other command first wait for the pending responses, so that none is executed after an error. Used by IScript.execute when SMT.Configuration.pipeline is set.

    • hasPending

      public boolean hasPending()
      Whether some pipelined command's response has not yet been read

    • readPipelined

      public void readPipelined(boolean wait)
      Reads what the solver has written for pipelined commands, matching each response to its command in order; with wait, until every pending command has its response (or the solver has stopped), else only what has already arrived. Standard error is checked each time output is read. Which command its text belongs to is not known while the solver runs, so it is kept until either the solver stops, when it becomes the response of the first command without one (as listen() would return it), or every pending response has been read, when it is logged as diagnostic output.

    • finishPipelined

    • set_option_impl

      protected IResponse set_option_impl(IExpr.IKeyword key, IAttributeValue value)
      Override in subclasses to handle solver-specific options. Channel options are handled by set_option and never reach here. This default handles :print-success client-side (see checkPrintSuccess(org.smtlib.SMT.Configuration, org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword, org.smtlib.IAttributeValue)): the solver process is always left with :print-success true at the wire level (see start()/sendCommand()) -- without that, we'd get no acknowledgment at all for other commands once a script turns it off -- so it is answered entirely client-side, matching the local smtConfig.nosuccess flag, and is never itself forwarded to the solver process. A subclass that overrides set_option_impl for other reasons (e.g. to also track option values locally) needs its own checkPrintSuccess call, same as it always has -- this default is only reached by a subclass that doesn't override set_option_impl at all.
